slot.brief: use the onto-function counting formula (inclusion–exclusion) to count surjections from an m-set onto an n-set

stem: The number of onto functions from a set with 6 elements to a set with 3 elements is
working:
Number of onto functions from set of size m to set of size n (n ≤ m) by inclusion–exclusion:
$$\sum_{r=0}^{n-1} (-1)^r \binom{n}{r} (n-r)^m.$$
For m = 6, n = 3:
$3^6 - \binom{3}{1}2^6 + \binom{3}{2}1^6 = 729 - 3 \times 64 + 3 \times 1 = 729 - 192 + 3 = 540.$
solution:
By inclusion–exclusion, the number of onto functions is
$$3^6-\binom{3}{1}2^6+\binom{3}{2}1^6=729-192+3=540.$$
